Organisation.description: Organisation information. All fields are optional.

Package.description: Package information. All fields are optional.

verification_id.description: Verification ID from a previous verification. (REQUIRED) Must exist in identity_verifications table and belong to the user associated with the organisation.

sign_with.description: Optional context fields to bind into the enclave signature. public_key is always signed implicitly and must not be included. Every requested field must resolve to a non-empty value, except key_fingerprint which may resolve after generation. Each field may only be listed once.

key_id.description: Unique identifier for the generated key (UUID)

signature.description: Base64 ECDSA P-256 DER signature. When sign_with is omitted, this signs the bare public_key hex; otherwise it signs signed_payload. Verify it with the verification key CoinCover issued you during integration, not with public_key.

signed_payload.description: RFC 8785 JCS-canonical JSON string signed by the enclave. Present only when sign_with was supplied. Verify its exact UTF-8 bytes without re-stringifying.

signed_fields.description: Validated context fields included in signed_payload, in request order. Does not include public_key. Present only when sign_with was supplied.

verification_id.description: Verification ID from a previous verification. (REQUIRED) Must exist in identity_verifications table and belong to the user associated with the organisation.

public_key.description: Public key in hexadecimal format. (REQUIRED) 32-4096 characters long.

backup.description: Array of backup items to store. (REQUIRED) Allows multiple pieces of data to be backed up in a single request. Limited to a maximum of 3 items.

item_key.description: Unique identifier for the backup item (e.g., "seed_phrase", "private_key", "wallet_config"). (REQUIRED)

item_checksum.description: SHA-256 hash of the data. (REQUIRED) 64 hex characters.

metadata.description: Optional metadata associated with the backup. Allows custom key-value pairs.

item_key.description: Unique identifier for the backup item (e.g., "seed_phrase", "private_key", "wallet_config"). Always present.

backup_id.description: Unique identifier for the stored backup (UUID format). Always present.

checksum.description: SHA-256 checksum of the stored data (echoed from request). Always present.

data_size.description: Size of the stored data in bytes. Always present.

backup_type.description: Type of backup. Always present. Value is always "data".

metadata.description: Metadata associated with the backup (echoed from request + enhanced with system metadata such as API key info, stored_at timestamp, and backup_items_count). Always present.

api_key_entity_type.description: Entity type from API key authorizer context

stored_at.description: ISO timestamp when backups were stored

backup_items_count.description: Number of backup items successfully stored

backup.description: Array of stored backup items. Each item contains the item_key, backup_id, checksum, and data_size.

verification_id.description: Verification ID from a successful verification. (REQUIRED) Must be approved/successful.

gpg_public_key.description: GPG public key in PGP public key block format for encrypting the recovered data. (REQUIRED)

-----BEGIN PGP PUBLIC KEY BLOCK-----
...
-----END PGP PUBLIC KEY BLOCK-----

oneOf.description: Direct RSA-OAEP encryption for small data

backup_id.description: Unique identifier for the backup (UUID format). Always present.

backup_item_key.description: Unique identifier for the backup item (e.g., "seed_phrase", "private_key", "wallet_config"). Present if available from metadata.

recovery_id.description: ID of the recovery record. Present if recovery was successful.

recovery_package.description: Recovery package containing the recovered data in encrypted format. Present if recovery was successful. Supports multiple encryption algorithms: GPG, RSA direct, or hybrid RSA-AES256-GCM.

original_filename.description: Original filename of the backup. Present if recovery was successful and filename was stored.

content_type.description: Content type of the backup. Present if recovery was successful and content type was stored.

original_size.description: Size of the original backup in bytes. Present if recovery was successful and size was stored.

metadata.description: Metadata associated with the backup. Present if metadata was stored.

error.description: Error message if recovery failed. Present only if recovery failed.

backup.description: Array of recovered backup items. Each item contains recovery information or error details.

post.description: Initiates a new identity verification workflow and returns a Verification ID. The user will use this verification_id to spin up a front-end SDK that will guide the user through the identity verification workflow.

get.description: Retrieves the current status of a biometric verification. The status can be in multiple states: 'pending' (initial state), 'approved' (all verifications passed), 'declined' (verifications failed), or 'review' (marked for manual review).

parameters.name: verification_id
parameters.description: Verification ID to check status for

post.description: Simulates biometric verification events for testing in non-production environments.

Generates a new cryptographic key for a user. Requires a user identifier and a verification_id that exists in the identity_verifications table and belongs to the user associated with the organisation. This endpoint calls the hot-keys orchestrator partner-assign-key endpoint.

Stores encrypted backup data securely. Accepts multiple backup items in a single request via the backup array (limited to a maximum of 3 items). Requires a verification_id that exists in the identity_verifications table and belongs to the user associated with the organisation. Each backup item's item_key (e.g., "seed_phrase", "private_key") is stored in the hot-keys database metadata as backup_item_key for recovery operations. This endpoint calls the hot-keys orchestrator partner-secure-data endpoint.

Recovers previously stored backup data. Requires successful identity verification (verification_id must be approved/successful). Requires a GPG public key for encrypting the recovered data. Returns an array of backup recovery results, each containing recovery information or error details. This endpoint calls the hot-keys orchestrator recover-backup endpoint for each backup associated with the user.
